clue.text: Difficult to get hold of drug, see?

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is a famous one

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a drug finds it slippery to obtain and asks you to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not the verb but a bishop's seat: the cathedral city of Ely is the crossword's favourite see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eel-like is slippery, so it is hard to grasp in the hand.

clue.text: Run in but only a little

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for run goes inside the word for but

parts.note: but, as in 'all but one', means except
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A batsman is told to take a run, but just a short one.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract, merely a small portion of a longer work.

clue.text: Topless woman of ill repute getting pulled at Northern club

indicators.note: topless says the word for the disreputable woman loses its first letter

parts.note: a slut is an old insult for a promiscuous woman
a car being pulled is on tow

explanation.surface: A scantily dressed woman of dubious reputation is being picked up at a nightclub up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a football club: Luton Town plays in Bedfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton Town is an English football club, named after its Bedfordshire home town.

clue.text: Poker player will be hoping for this many

definitions.text: Poker player will be hoping for this
definitions.meaning: a card player hopes the dealer gives a strong hand, a good deal of the cards
many as a quantity, plenty, lots

explanation.surface: A card player at the poker table hopes for plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a large amount, and punningly a fine deal of cards for a poker player.

clue.text: The carnivores of Kelly Eliot?

parts.note: Gene Kelly, the American dancer and film star
T. S. Eliot, the poet, known by his initials

explanation.surface: A question about which meat-eaters belong to someone called Kelly Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelly Eliot looks like one person's name, but it is two surnames: the first names Gene and T.S. go with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Genets are small cat-like carnivorous mammals of Africa and southern Europe.

clue.text: Giving a miss a quid, going through sale jumble

indicators.note: going through says one piece sits inside the other
a jumble mixes things up, so the letters of sale are rearranged

parts.note: a quid of tobacco is a piece for chewing, a chew

explanation.surface: Someone skips a sale because each item costs a pound and it is all a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quid' looks like a pound coin but is a plug of chewing tobacco; 'jumble' rearranges the sale's letters as ESAL, split by 'going through'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschewal is the act of avoiding something, the noun from eschew, to shun.

clue.text: Sod the story books! Get in a bookmaker

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
an account is a story or narrative
NT stands for New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An angry outburst against the storybooks, followed by a call to visit the bookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sod' looks like an expletive but means a clod of grass; 'the' and 'Get in' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf accountant is a jocular British name for a bookie who takes bets on horse races.

clue.text: Fragrant substance boxed by genteel emir

indicators.note: boxed by says the answer is held inside the following words

explanation.surface: A refined Arab ruler keeps a perfumed substance in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Cheek! Decline to speak for work on sound-track

parts.note: lip means insolent talk, cheek

indicators.note: to speak says a word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to decline is to sink, as in falling standards

explanation.surface: An insolent remark, then a refusal to say anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline to speak' reads as refusing to talk, but 'Decline' is SINK and 'to speak' means its sound, SYNC.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-sync is to mouth words in time with a recorded track, as singers do on TV.

clue.text: Part of leg hurts? I will stay in — keep nursing!

indicators.note: stay in says the contraction sits inside the word for hurts

parts.note: something that hurts aches
I will contracts to I'll
to tend is to nurse, and to keep on doing so is tend on

explanation.surface: A patient with a painful leg vows to remain in hospital and have the nursing continue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscles to the heel bone at the back of the leg.

clue.text: 3D image that musical is able to produce

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A stage musical is said to be capable of producing a three-dimensional picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A CAT scan is computerised tomography, building cross-sectional images of the body.

clue.text: Knife injury obtained from disorganised rave in hollow

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters go inside the word for hollow

parts.note: a cup is a hollow vessel or depression

indicators.note: disorganised means jumbled, so the letters of rave are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stabbing occurred at a chaotic all-night dance in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up in slang is a slashing with a blade, from carving someone up.

clue.text: Is typical of Bradman & Son?

definitions.meaning: a trait that is common among relatives is typical of the household
Don Bradman, the great Australian batsman, scored runs, and with his son the scoring is within the household

explanation.surface: A question whether the great cricketer and his son typify something.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman was Australia's legendary Test batsman, so cricket runs would be a family business.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a quality is inherited and shared by relatives, so is characteristic of them.

clue.text: Drive along nearly as far as town in West Yorkshire?

parts.note: to, as in 'from here to there', means as far as

indicators.note: nearly says the place name loses its final letter

parts.note: Otley is a market town in West Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A motorist drives almost all the way to a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Otley is a small market town near Leeds; 'nearly' drops its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is to drive or travel along in a leisurely, unhurried way.

clue.text: Sleep-inducing oils initially detected in Northern ocean

indicators.note: detected in says the picked letter is found inside the ocean's name

parts.note: the Arctic is the northernmost ocean

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of oils

explanation.surface: Soporific oil slicks are spotted in a northern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic drug dulls the senses and brings on drowsiness or sleep.

clue.text: Character instructing musician's touched round old woman up!

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the built word is read from bottom to top
round says the word for touched goes around the old woman

parts.note: felt is the past tense of feel, to touch
a crone is a withered old woman

explanation.surface: A musician has been touched and rounds on an old woman in excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touched' poses as emotional, but it is a past tense; 'up' turns the assembled FELCRONET backwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is a symbol telling a player the pitch of the staff, so it instructs the musician.

clue.text: One's dying to be a source of annoyance

definitions.meaning: one who is dying is one who perishes
British slang for an annoying person, often a child

explanation.surface: Someone at death's door is also a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Perisher is British informal for a pest, and literally one who perishes.

clue.text: One doing service in church

definitions.meaning: a clergyman who conducts a church service
a large or important church, such as York's

explanation.surface: Someone serving in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister leads worship, and a minster is also the name of a great church such as Westminster.

clue.text: Companion seeking fortune as a sailor

parts.note: a mate is a companion or friend
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A friend goes off to seek his fortune at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British informal for a seaman, from the French word for sailor.

clue.text: Having soured, artist shortly died

indicators.note: shortly says the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: J. M. W. Turner, the English painter

explanation.surface: An embittered painter dies soon afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that has turned has gone sour.

clue.text: One who arranges the kitchen sideboard

definitions.meaning: someone who dresses a shop window or a stage arranges things
a kitchen cabinet with shelves above for plates

explanation.surface: A person who sets out the kitchen furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is one who dresses or arranges, and also a sideboard with shelves for crockery.

clue.text: Sign outside a National Trust building

indicators.note: outside says the zodiac sign wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A sign put up outside a National Trust property.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses in Britain, often abbreviated NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or building propped against a wall.

clue.text: Cheers high-scoring draw your newspaper's covered

indicators.note: covered says the newspaper's name is enclosed by the score

parts.note: three-three is a high draw in a football match
the clue appears in The Times, so your paper is the Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports a celebration of a goal-filled drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your newspaper' is the paper you are reading, The Times; 'covered' looks like reporting but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times three is a round of three cheers repeated three times.

clue.text: One who's got up an additional clause

definitions.meaning: one who has mounted a horse or bicycle
an amendment added to a document or bill

explanation.surface: Someone who has stood up adds an extra clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is one who rides on a mount, and also a clause appended to a legal document.

clue.text: Took pulse after reversing over one's superior in carriage

indicators.note: over says the pair goes around the letter for one
reversing says the combined pair is read backwards
after says the pulse follows took

parts.note: took means had, as in had a meal
dal is a dish of lentils or other pulses
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone's heart rate is measured after backing a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns HADDAL into LADDAH, and 'over' wraps that around I.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-dah describes affectedly genteel or snooty manners, a superior bearing.

clue.text: Get confused about place, in turning paper

indicators.note: in says the two short pieces go inside the reversed paper
turning says the paper's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
on means about, as in a talk on art
pl is the abbreviation for place, as in addresses

explanation.surface: Someone muddled while turning the pages of a newspaper looking for a place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; 'turning' makes NUS, which opens to take the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus is to get someone confused, leaving them perplexed and at a loss.

clue.text: Where the king sits, by emperor who fiddled with order

parts.note: by, as in 'by way of', means through, shortened thro
Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A monarch sits beside a Roman ruler who tinkered with the seating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' looks like an anagram signal but completes Nero's description; the OM is a British order of merit.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne room is the state room containing a monarch's throne.

clue.text: A ranch, miles away? Miles away!

indicators.note: miles away says the abbreviation M for miles is removed

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A distant ranch is described as remote.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats 'Miles away': first as an instruction to drop M, then as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, far off.
